gloss: to drive in; to devote oneself to; to type in

definitions.gloss: to drive in; to hammer in
definitions.explanation: To strike something so that it goes into a surface.

definitions.gloss: to devote oneself to; to be absorbed in
definitions.explanation: To dedicate oneself wholeheartedly to an activity or pursuit.
To enter data or text into a computer or device.

examples.japanese: {壁|かべ}に{釘|くぎ}を{打|う}ち{込|こ}んだ。
examples.english: I drove a nail into the wall.

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}は{研究|けんきゅう}に{打|う}ち{込|こ}んでいる。
examples.english: She is devoted to her research.

examples.japanese: パスワードを{打|う}ち{込|こ}んでください。

notes:
{打|う}ち{込|こ}む is a transitive verb ({他動詞|たどうし}) formed from {打|う}つ (to strike) + {込|こ}む (into). It has evolved from physical striking to include figurative devotion and modern computer input.

ASPECT (ている):
- {打|う}ち{込|こ}んでいる (physical): something is embedded
- {打|う}ち{込|こ}んでいる (devotion): is absorbed in, devoted to

PARTICLE PATTERNS:
- [nail]を[surface]に{打|う}ち{込|こ}む — to drive [nail] into [surface]
- [activity]に{打|う}ち{込|こ}む — to devote oneself to [activity]
- [data]を{打|う}ち{込|こ}む — to type in [data]

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {仕事|しごと}に{打|う}ち{込|こ}む (devote oneself to work)
- {練習|れんしゅう}に{打|う}ち{込|こ}む (throw oneself into practice)
- データを{打|う}ち{込|こ}む (input data)
- {杭|くい}を{打|う}ち{込|こ}む (drive in a stake)

NOTE: For the "devote oneself" meaning, the particle is に (intransitive use), while for physical/typing meanings, it takes を (transitive).
